title: Count Words Obtained After Adding a Letter
summary: Given two arrays of strings, startWords and targetWords, each containing lowercase English letters, count how many strings in targetWords can be formed by appending a unique lowercase letter to a string in startWords and then rearranging its letters.
statement: Given two arrays of strings, startWords and targetWords, each containing lowercase English letters, count how many strings in targetWords can be formed by appending a unique lowercase letter to a string in startWords and then rearranging its letters. The appended letter must not already be present in the string from startWords. The order of letters in the resulting string does not need to match the original order.
constraints: Letters within every word are distinct lowercase characters.
A target qualifies when removing exactly one of its letters yields the letter set of a start word; rearrangement is allowed.
hints: Distinct letters allow each word to be represented by a 26-bit set mask.
Store all start masks; for each target, remove each one-bit in turn and test membership.
Count target once if any target_mask XOR letter_bit belongs to the start set.
Removing one target letter exactly reverses the allowed append-and-rearrange operation, and masks ignore irrelevant order.
editorial: Removing one target letter exactly reverses the allowed append-and-rearrange operation, and masks ignore irrelevant order.

tests.explanation: tack comes from act plus k and acti from act plus i, so two targets qualify.
abc can come from ab; the other targets cannot be formed by one addition.
